newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam expects jump in aid pledges - report.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam expects jump in aid pledges - report.

text.p: Vietnam expects the donor community to pledge aid worth $2.8 billion at a World Bank consultative group meeting in Hanoi next month, the Saigon Times Daily reported on Monday.

"The External Relations Division of the Ministry of Planning and Investment...believes that donor countries will commit to providing some $2.8 billion for Vietnam at the forthcoming get-together," the state-controlled newspaper said.
Donors have become increasingly sympathetic to communist Vietnam since the leadership embarked on a reform process and a more open-door foreign policy in the late 1980s.
Aid commitments came to $1.8 billion in 1993, $1.9 billion in 1994 and $2.31 billion last year.
The consultative group meetings, donor gatherings for poor countries chaired by the World Bank, are usually held in Paris.
But this year's meeting for Vietnam will be held in Hanoi, on December 5 and 6, to allow the authorities to give a full explanation of a new five-year economic plan.
In a report ratified at the Communist Party's landmark congress two months ago, the government set a target of average economic growth of 9-10 percent a year between now and 2000.
The report pledged to continue with reforms of the centrally planned economy, which have brought vigorous growth of more than eight percent annually since 1992.
